notes: Solid implementation: squashfs lookup and root handling stay consistent and squashfs Open clamps the range; the zip-only special case for seeking a symlink past its end is a bit ad hoc but harmless, and the end-to-end tests cover copying, escape and regular .rclonelink files.

Works and passes, but adds an unnecessary symlink-only offset/EOF special case in zip `Open` and changes the squashfs single-root check for all files. The escape test only logs the copy error rather than asserting it.

Code matches the reference fix exactly: the zip suffix is added before root filtering, squashfs List and NewObject name entries the same way, and squashfs Open clamps the offset; it adds good end-to-end tests including the hostile-archive escape, plus a small relevant docs section.

Code is effectively identical to the reference for zip and squashfs, plus a relevant docs section and tests for squashfs listing/reading and the hostile-zip copy. The zip unit test is thinner and skips range reads and regular `.rclonelink` members.

Correct for both backends: NewObject retries with the suffix trimmed and checks that remotes match, the squashfs single-object root is handled, and safety relies on the local backend as the reference does; tests are thorough, with minor nits such as the dropped allRemotes doc comment and os.Chdir in a test.

Correct and fairly clean implementation for both backends, with consistent NewObject and List naming and good tests (zip, copy, escape, go-diskfs squashfs). Minor issues: `objectFromFileInfo` doubles as the links gate, it relies on an interface assertion for `Readlink`, and a doc comment was lost in the test file.

Reads the flag from VFS.Opt.Links rather than fs.GetConfig(ctx).Links, which is non-idiomatic and also triggers on --vfs-links; it restructures readZip into two passes and silently drops regular files nested under symlinks without counting them, so CopyDir succeeds instead of erroring in the escape test.

Reads the flag from `VFS.Opt.Links` instead of the `-l/--links` config, and heavily restructures `readZip` to hide members below symlinks and drop colliding links. That diverges from the expected behaviour (fails a hidden test) and adds considerable complexity.

Zip side matches the reference; on squashfs the new linkName parameter and findObjectNative make lookups convoluted, rooting at a hidden symlink yields an odd empty directory Fs, CopyN seeking past the end errors, and a test comment is truncated.

The zip change is correct and close to the reference. The squashfs side works but is convoluted: a `linkName` parameter, a `findObjectNative` wrapper and fiddly single-root logic, and seeking past the end of a link returns an error instead of clamping.

Covers zip and squashfs, but over-engineered: it adds a two-pass zip filter that silently drops members under symlinks (failing the end-to-end escape test that expects an error), runs hasSymlinkAncestor ReadDir walks on every List/NewObject, makes New return ErrorObjectNotFound for some roots, and a squashfs seek past the end returns an error.

Adds an expensive per-call `hasSymlinkAncestor` directory walk and makes squashfs `New` fail outright when root names a symlink. Zip filtering is complex: it hides nested members and drops same-named regular files but misses suffix collisions, and it fails a hidden test.

Adds a new shared archiver LinkFilter with case-insensitive clash rules that can hide regular .rclonelink members (contrary to the spec), makes squashfs NewObject build the whole directory listing, and broadens scope well beyond the task.

Over-engineered: a new shared `LinkFilter` file, case-insensitive clash filtering, and squashfs `NewObject` now computing every directory entry's info. It can drop a regular `.rclonelink` member on a clash, contrary to the spec, and fails a hidden test.

Thoughtful clash and nesting handling that keeps regular files and drops conflicting symlinks, but it eagerly decompresses link targets at mount time and makes notable structural changes; dropping the link instead of letting the copy error diverges from the expected escape behaviour.

Core translation works, but it eagerly reads every zip link target, pokes at dirtree internals, logs per clash entry, and drops symlinks with nested members rather than following the expected behaviour. It fails a hidden test.

Identical to the reference fix: it stops leaking dup'd fds, unlinks Addr().String() under the lock, adds a CAS double-close returning ErrClosed, and handles abstract sockets. Tests are thorough across unix and unixgram, double close, the concurrent relisten race, and abstract sentinels.

The source change is essentially identical to the reference: it closes the dup'd socketFile, takes the mutex in Close, unlinks using the Addr name, and adds CAS-based net.ErrClosed handling and the abstract-socket guard. The tests are thorough, covering both networks, double close, refcounting and the close/listen race.

Fixes the root cause: a persistent dup'd fd is closed on the last release, the real path is unlinked, double close returns ErrClosed, and abstract sockets are skipped. However, it also changes the return value of fakeCloseListener.Close in listen.go, which is the non-unix path and unrelated to this issue, and edits listen_test.go to match; hidden tests fail because they rely on internal fields such as count.

The shared-state redesign (owned fd, refcount, lock held through Close, identity-checked map delete) is behaviourally sound and handles all the listed edge cases. However, it also changes fakeCloseListener and fakeClosePacketConn in listen.go and edits listen_test.go, which alters non-unix close semantics outside the task.

A holder-set design that always dups from a live holder; it fixes the leak and unlink, guards double close, and handles the race under the lock. The approach is somewhat unusual, the abstract check is not OS-gated, and the race test runs only once while the abstract test writes into the package directory.

A holder-set design copies the fd from any still-open holder and closes the temporary file, with all mutation under unixSocketsMu. This correctly fixes the leak, unlinking, double close and the race. It changes internal types (map type, pointer deleteListener), its abstract check ignores GOOS, and its race test runs only one iteration.

Semantically close to the reference: closes the dup'd file, unlinks via Addr, adds a CAS double-close guard, and serializes close under unixSocketsMu with an abstract check. It also changes reused sockets to be wrapped in *deleteListener with listenerPool accounting, which breaks the hidden tests' type assertions; it keeps the reference's stale-closed-map-entry weakness.

The core fix matches the reference: it closes the dup'd file, serialises close under unixSocketsMu, unlinks via Addr(), uses a CAS for double close and skips abstract names. However, it also wraps reused sockets in a pointer deleteListener and changes listenerPool/ListenerUsage accounting, which was not asked for and breaks the hidden tests at runtime; its abstract-name check also omits android.

A sound refcounted unixSocket design with a persistent fd and a separate state mutex; it correctly handles the close/listen race, the newest-holder-closed case, and abstract paths. The diff is large: it restructures listenReusable, edits listeners.go, and changes listenerPool accounting, and the hidden tests fail from internal API coupling.

This appears correct, using a refcounted shared fd and an unlink only while the socket is still current in the map. It adds a second mutex, heavily refactors listenReusable, changes listenerPool accounting for reused sockets and edits listeners.go. That makes it the most invasive candidate; the tests are strong.

A clean shared-state unixSocket (file, path, refs) guarded by the existing mutex: the last release closes the fd and unlinks, the abstract check is OS-gated, double close yields ErrClosed, and reuse after the newest holder closes also works. Its tests are excellent (including a pending-connection-dropped check); the hidden tests fail only because internal fields were renamed.

This restructures tracking into a shared unixSocket that keeps its own dup'd fd and a mutex-guarded refcount. It fixes the leaked File() dups, unlinks the path, handles double close, the close/listen race, abstract names, and even the newest-holder-closed-first case. It also rewrites the map type, drops the count field and changes deleteListener to a pointer type, which is more invasive than needed and is likely why the hidden tests fail to build.
